searchText: For a context for others. We discussed execution payload dissemination strategy for Hegota as part of Phase 1 BiB (EIP-8142). We agreed that for the payload we can apply erasure coding + merkle commitment which can go into execution bid. The exact networking scheme (PeerDAS style columns subnets vs single subnet) is still TBD. We will explore it more in the coming days. More details are here: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12072 Gm cl devs. Regarding [EIP-8146](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8146) (BAL Sidecars, pfi'd for hegota) I was chatting with <@628018527470616606> and we thought it would be best if CLs make sure to always pass the BAL before the payload to the EL. ELs cannot really do anything with the payload alone and need the BAL for execution. So, when the payload arrives before the BAL, either the CL or the EL would need to cache the payload while waiting for the BAL. If we do that on the CL, then the CL would just have to make sure to never call `engine_newPayloadV*` before having called `engine_notifyBlockAccessListV1` . The response from the EL to newPayload would stay the same as today. This seems like the best solution. If we do it on the EL, then we might need new responses to newPayload, e.g. MISSING_BAL. Clarified in this PR: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12216 CC <@592004585506340885> <@425572898787426305> Not sure if this is the right channel but my 2cents about this EIP is that it's very naive to expect builders to release any information about their payload early. Bals include state changes and I don't see why builders will have any incentive to deliver that earlier than the list of transactions have been made public Eip-8146 How is one or the other entity buffering this substantively different, i.e. why affirmatively require this? ELs have to have some handling regardless, even if the handling is, well, the spec prohibits this `engine_notifyBlockAccessListV1`/`engine_newPayloadV*` ordering I think it only matters when we want to keep the response of newPayload the same, not having to introduce a new response like bal_missing. With the order being set by the CL, the EL can always assume the bal is cached when the payload arrives. does that mean the payload can never be validated without BAL? how should CL behave in the case when BAL isn't received at all? EIP-8383 Payload Validation without BAL

excerpts.author: .just_kk
excerpts.content:
For a context for others. 
We discussed execution payload dissemination strategy for Hegota as part of Phase 1 BiB (EIP-8142).

We agreed that for the payload we can apply erasure coding + merkle commitment which can go into execution bid.

The exact networking scheme (PeerDAS style columns subnets vs single subnet) is still TBD. We will explore it more in the coming days.

More details are here:
https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12072

excerpts.author: nero_eth
excerpts.content:
Gm cl devs. Regarding [EIP-8146](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8146) (BAL Sidecars, pfi'd for hegota) I was chatting with <@628018527470616606> and we thought it would be best if CLs make sure to always pass the BAL before the payload to the EL. 
ELs cannot really do anything with the payload alone and need the BAL for execution. 
So, when the payload arrives before the BAL, either the CL or the EL would need to cache the payload while waiting for the BAL.

If we do that on the CL, then the CL would just have to make sure to never call `engine_newPayloadV*` before having called `engine_notifyBlockAccessListV1` . The response from the EL to newPayload would stay the same as today. This seems like the best solution.

If we do it on the EL, then we might need new responses to newPayload, e.g. MISSING_BAL.

Clarified in this PR: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12216
CC <@592004585506340885> <@425572898787426305>

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Not sure if this is the right channel but my 2cents about this EIP is that it's very naive to expect builders to release any information about their payload early. Bals include state changes and I don't see why builders will have any incentive to deliver that earlier than the list of transactions have been made public

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: How is one or the other entity buffering this substantively different, i.e. why affirmatively require this?

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: ELs have to have some handling regardless, even if the handling is, well, the spec prohibits this `engine_notifyBlockAccessListV1`/`engine_newPayloadV*` ordering

excerpts.author: nero_eth
excerpts.content:
I think it only matters when we want to keep the response of newPayload the same, not having to introduce a new response like bal_missing.
With the order being set by the CL, the EL can always assume the bal is cached when the payload arrives.
